On 06/26/2025 at about 19:30, a caller phoned 911 to report a vehicle driving in circles in the parking lot at 2400 E Sample Blvd. The caller, Taylor, advised the vehicle parked and the driver appeared slumped. He also informed that he could smell Fentanyl coming from the car. 
I arrived and noticed the described vehicle on the west side of the Chipotle. I could see the back of the driver's head tilted forward into the steering wheel. The lights on the car began to flash on and off. The door opened slowly and the driver stepped out appearing off balance and stumbled as he made several attempts to put keys into a backpack. I contacted Alex Morgan. He appeared confused and I could smell the distinct odor of burnt Fentanyl on his clothing. He continued to fumble at his backpack and I detained him with handcuffs while I waited for backup. 
I advised Morgan that I had responded due to a call for service about him driving in circles in the parking lot. Morgan advised that he worked at the Chipotle and he had not been driving in circles. I asked if he had been using anything and Morgan said, \"Yeah but...\" and trailed off. 
I noted Morgan was wearing a hooded sweatshirt although it was hot. His eyes appeared in the normal DRE range but were not adjusting to my flashlight as I would expect. Officer Sample 654321 arrived. I removed Morgan's handcuffs and administered HGN. (0/6) Next, I conducted the Walk and Turn using a painted parking line. The One Leg Stand was completed in the same location. (2/6,3/4) The OLS was stopped because I thought he might fall. 
Morgan agreed to answer my questions. He admitted to using Fentanyl and stated he has a 10 pill a day habit. He advised that he had not used since the day before. I noted a slow slurred speech pattern and he appeared drowsy. I instructed the Modified Romberg and Morgan counted to 19 seconds and advised it was 30 seconds. 
Morgan submitted to a Preliminary Breath Test which read his BrAC as 0.000 at 19:55. I placed Morgan under arrest for DUI at 19:57. 
He declined a chemical test. I read the APS/IC Admonitions and he changed his mind. Morgan advised that he had poor veins. After checking Morgan's arms I wished to have the use of an Accuvein. Officer Sample transported Morgan to the westside substation. Morgan signed the blood draw consent form. I was unsuccessful with blood collection, but Morgan agreed to providing a urine sample the sample was collected and sealed into a urine kit. The urine kit, along with the paraphernalia I discovered in Morgan's backpack, were placed into evidence. 
Due to citywide computer outage this case never attached through AXON the evidence was manually entered into BEAST at the station. 
I completed a Drug Influence Evaluation: See report.
